parts.title: Multiple choice (Questions 1–50)
parts.instructions: This paper has 50 multiple choice questions (1 to 50). Each question has 4 choices. Choose ONE best answer and blacken its letter on the separate answer sheet.

source.document: raw/2014-Science-V-A.pdf (7 pages: cover + questions on pp. 2-7, 'THE END' after Q50)
source.other_version: raw/2014-Science-V-B.pdf – same 50 questions, reordered and with shuffled options; used only to check the text.
source.notes: Cover: 'End-of-Basic Education (Grade 8) National Examination, Eritrea, 2014 – 4. Science – Version A'. Text from the PDF text layer, checked against the page images. Figures cropped at 250 dpi: Fig.1 water changes of state (Q5), Fig.2 tongue taste regions (Q10), Fig.3 respiratory system (Q14), Fig.4 blood-flow diagram (Q16), Fig.5 thermometer in water (Q26-27), Fig.6 female reproductive organs (Q34). The cell table in Q9 is typed as a stem table.
source.printing_note: Clean digital print. Small slips in the paper: Q31 option B says 'cow is a producer' although the chain has a sheep (no effect on the answer); Q24 'slopping' for 'sloping'; Q27 '(0F)' = °F.

exam.answer_key_note: No official key. Answers solved and checked against the Eritrean MoE Grade 6–8 textbooks.

questions.stem: Which of the following is SI unit of mass?
explanation_steps: SI units: mass – kilogram (kg); time – second (s); length – metre (m).
An hour is a unit of time. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 9)
questions.explain_simple: Mass is measured in kilograms.
tips: SI units: kg (mass), m (length), s (time).

similar_questions.stem: Which instrument measures mass?
explanation_steps: A beam balance measures mass in kilograms or grams.

questions.stem: Matter is defined as anything that occupies space and has
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'Matter is anything that occupies space and has mass.'
Many kinds of matter (like air or water) have no colour, taste or smell, but all matter has mass. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Matter takes up space and has mass.
tips: Matter = mass + takes up space.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is NOT matter?
explanation_steps: Light has no mass and does not take up space. It is energy, not matter.

questions.stem: The type of teeth with sharp edges used for biting or cutting solid foods is:
explanation_steps: Incisors are the flat front teeth with sharp edges. They bite and cut food.
Canines tear food; premolars and molars crush and grind food. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 6)
questions.explain_simple: The front teeth (incisors) cut and bite food.
tips: Incisors cut, canines tear, premolars and molars grind.

similar_questions.stem: Which teeth are used for grinding food?
explanation_steps: Molars are the big back teeth. They grind food.

questions.stem: Burning and rusting are examples of
explanation_steps: In a chemical change a new substance is formed and the change is hard to reverse.
Burning makes ash and gases; rusting makes rust from iron, water and oxygen. Both make new substances.
So they are chemical changes. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 43)
questions.explain_simple: Burning and rusting make new substances. They are chemical changes.
tips: New substance → chemical change. Same substance (just shape or state changes) → physical change.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a physical change?
explanation_steps: Melting ice is still water. No new substance forms, so it is a physical change.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 3 – Properties and Changes of Matter

questions.stem: Figure 1 shows the processes that occur when water changes from one state of matter to other. The processes are labeled 1, 2, 3 and 4. Which process is represented by 2?
questions.image_alt: Figure 1: a circle of arrows. Arrow 1 goes from liquid water (left) up to steam (top); arrow 2 from steam down to liquid water (right); arrow 4 from that liquid water down to an ice cube (bottom); arrow 3 from the ice cube up to the liquid water on the left.
explanation_steps: Arrow 1: liquid water → steam (boiling). Arrow 2: steam → liquid water. Arrow 4: liquid water → ice (freezing). Arrow 3: ice → liquid water (melting).
Gas (steam) changing to liquid is condensation (condensing). Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 49)
questions.explain_simple: Arrow 2 goes from steam to liquid water. That is condensing.
tips: Gas → liquid = condensation; liquid → gas = boiling/evaporation.

similar_questions.stem: In the same figure, which process is arrow 3 (ice → liquid water)?
explanation_steps: Solid ice changing to liquid water is melting.

questions.stem: Which of the following properties is true about air?
explanation_steps: Air is a gas. We cannot see it.
A gas has no definite shape and no definite volume: it fills any container.
But air is matter, so it occupies (takes up) space. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 84)
questions.explain_simple: Air takes up space, even though we cannot see it.
tips: Gases: no fixed shape, no fixed volume, but they take up space and have mass.

similar_questions.stem: When you blow into a balloon, it gets bigger. This shows that air
explanation_steps: The air inside takes up space, so the balloon gets bigger.

questions.stem: An eclipse that takes place when the moon passes between the Sun and the Earth is:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'A solar eclipse takes place when the moon passes between the sun and the earth.'
The Moon blocks the sunlight, so the Sun is hidden (eclipse of the sun).
A lunar eclipse (eclipse of the moon) happens when the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: When the Moon is between the Sun and the Earth, it hides the Sun. This is a solar eclipse.
tips: Solar eclipse: Sun – Moon – Earth. Lunar eclipse: Sun – Earth – Moon.

similar_questions.stem: A lunar eclipse happens when

options.A: the Moon is between the Sun and the Earth
options.B: the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon
options.C: the Sun is between the Earth and the Moon
options.D: the Moon is very near the Sun

explanation_steps: The Earth's shadow falls on the Moon when the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly shows the level of increasing organization in the human body?

options.A: cells → tissues → organs → systems → human body
options.B: systems → cells → tissues → organs → human body
options.C: human body → systems → organs → tissues → cells
options.D: cells → systems → tissues → organs → human body

explanation_steps: Similar cells form a tissue. Different tissues form an organ. Organs that work together form a system. All systems form the body (organism).
From the smallest to the largest: cells → tissues → organs → systems → human body. Answer: A.
(C is the same list but in decreasing order.)
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 107-108)
questions.explain_simple: Cells make tissues, tissues make organs, organs make systems, and systems make the body.
tips: Small to big: cell – tissue – organ – system – organism.

similar_questions.stem: A group of similar cells doing the same job is called
explanation_steps: Similar cells working together form a tissue, like muscle tissue.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 7 – Structure and Function in Living Things

questions.stem: The Table below provides some information on three types of cells, P, Q and R. The tick (√) indicates the presence of the part of the cell. Which of them is most likely an animal cell?
explanation_steps: Animal cells have a nucleus and a cell membrane but NO cell wall and NO chloroplasts.
Cell P has only a nucleus and a cell membrane. So P is an animal cell.
Q has a cell wall and chloroplasts (a green plant cell). R has a cell wall (a plant cell without chloroplasts, for example a root cell). Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 104)
questions.explain_simple: Cell P has no cell wall and no chloroplast. So it is an animal cell.
tips: Cell wall or chloroplast present → plant cell.

similar_questions.stem: A cell has a cell wall, chloroplasts, a nucleus and a cell membrane. It is most likely
explanation_steps: Chloroplasts and a cell wall show a plant cell, like a leaf cell.

questions.stem: Figure 2 shows the four taste regions of the tongue. The region that detects bitter taste is:
questions.image_alt: Figure 2: outline of a tongue with dashed lines dividing it into regions. Label 1 is the back part, 2 the sides, 3 a band near the front, and 4 the tip.
explanation_steps: In the textbook tongue map (Grade 6, Fig. 8.5): the back of the tongue is bitter, the sides are sour, the front sides are salt and the tip is sweet.
In Figure 2, region 1 is the back part of the tongue. So region 1 detects bitter taste. Answer: D.
(Region 2 = sour, 3 = salt, 4 = sweet.)
questions.explain_simple: The back of the tongue (region 1) tastes bitter things.
tips: Tongue map: tip sweet, front sides salt, sides sour, back bitter.

similar_questions.stem: In the same tongue map, which region detects sweet taste?
explanation_steps: The tip of the tongue detects sweet taste in the textbook map.

textbook_ref.topic: 8.2 Response to external stimuli (skin, tongue, nose)
textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.section: 8.2 Response to external stimuli (skin, tongue, nose)

questions.review_flag: Outdated fact: the 'tongue map' (each taste only in one region) is taught in the Grade 6 textbook (Fig. 8.5), but modern science shows every part of the tongue can sense all tastes. Answer keyed from the textbook map.

questions.stem: Nura has a mass of 35 kg. What is her weight on Earth if the earth's gravity is 10 N/kg?
explanation_steps: Weight = mass × gravity (W = m × g).
W = 35 kg × 10 N/kg = 350 N. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 25)
questions.explain_simple: Weight = 35 × 10 = 350 newtons.
tips: Weight (N) = mass (kg) × g (10 N/kg on Earth).

similar_questions.stem: A bag has a mass of 4 kg. What is its weight on Earth (g = 10 N/kg)?

questions.stem: The joint found between the head and vertebrae that allows nodding or turning movements is:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'The pivot joint found between the head and vertebrae…' It lets the head turn and nod.
Hinge joints are in the elbow and knee; ball and socket joints in the hip and shoulder. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: The joint that turns the head is the pivot joint.
tips: Pivot = turning (head on the neck).

similar_questions.stem: Which joint is found in the shoulder?
explanation_steps: The shoulder has a ball and socket joint, so the arm moves in all directions.

questions.stem: Which human organ system creates sex cells and offspring?
explanation_steps: The reproductive system makes sex cells (sperm and eggs) and allows people to have children (offspring).
Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 23)
questions.explain_simple: The reproductive system makes sex cells and babies.
tips: Reproduce = make new young ones.

similar_questions.stem: The male reproductive organs that make sperm are the
explanation_steps: The testes produce sperm cells.

questions.stem: Which human organ system is shown in Figure 3?
questions.image_alt: Figure 3: side view of a head with the nose and mouth, a tube (trachea) going down into the chest, branching into two dark lungs.
explanation_steps: The figure shows the nose and mouth, the windpipe (trachea), the bronchi and two lungs.
These are the organs of breathing: the respiratory system. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 11-12)
questions.explain_simple: The picture shows the lungs and windpipe. That is the respiratory system.
tips: Lungs in the picture → respiratory system.

similar_questions.stem: Air passes from the nose to the lungs through the
explanation_steps: The trachea (windpipe) carries air to the lungs.

questions.stem: The type of blood cells used to defend the body against germs that cause diseases are:
explanation_steps: White blood cells defend (protect) the body against germs.
Red blood cells carry oxygen; platelets help clotting; plasma is the liquid part. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 18)
questions.explain_simple: White blood cells fight germs.
tips: White = fighters (defence).

similar_questions.stem: Which part of blood carries oxygen?
explanation_steps: Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to the body.

questions.stem: The arrows in Figure 4 show how blood flows in human body. Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.image_alt: Figure 4: three boxes: Lungs (top), Heart (middle), Parts of the body (bottom). Arrow 1 on the left goes from the heart up to the lungs; arrow 2 on the right goes from the lungs down to the heart; arrow 4 on the right goes from the heart down to the body; arrow 3 on the left goes from the body up to the heart.

options.A: the blood at 1 contains more oxygen than the blood at 2.
options.B: the blood at 1 contains less oxygen than the blood at 4.
options.C: the blood at 2 contains more carbon dioxide than the blood at 3.

explanation_steps: Follow the arrows: 1 goes from the heart to the lungs; 2 goes from the lungs back to the heart; 4 goes from the heart to the parts of the body; 3 comes back from the body to the heart.
Blood gets oxygen in the lungs. So the blood at 2 and 4 is rich in oxygen. The blood at 1 and 3 is poor in oxygen and rich in carbon dioxide.
A is false (1 has less oxygen than 2). C is false (2 has less carbon dioxide than 3). B is true: blood at 1 has less oxygen than blood at 4. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 20-22)
questions.explain_simple: Blood at 1 goes to the lungs to get oxygen. Blood at 4 already has oxygen. So 1 has less oxygen than 4.
tips: Blood after the lungs = oxygen-rich. Blood after the body = oxygen-poor.

similar_questions.stem: In Figure 4, which blood contains the most carbon dioxide?
explanation_steps: Blood at 3 returns from the body parts, where cells gave it carbon dioxide.

questions.stem:
The force of an object can be determined by using the equation below.
Force = mass x acceleration
Which object would have the greatest force?

options.A: a 5 Kg object accelerating at 10 m/s²
options.B: a 5 Kg object accelerating at 20 m/s²
options.C: a 20 Kg object accelerating at 4 m/s²
options.D: a 20 Kg object accelerating at 3 m/s²

explanation_steps: Work out F = m × a for each.
The greatest is 100 N. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 60-61)
questions.explain_simple: Multiply mass by acceleration for each. B gives 100 N, the biggest.
tips: Calculate every option before you choose.

similar_questions.stem: What force is needed to give a 2 kg ball an acceleration of 6 m/s²?

questions.stem: A student pushes against a tree with a force of 10 N. The tree does not move. What is the amount of force exerted by the tree on the student?
explanation_steps: Newton's third law: for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.
The student pushes the tree with 10 N (action). The tree pushes back on the student with 10 N (reaction), in the opposite direction.
Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 65)
questions.explain_simple: The tree pushes back with the same force: 10 N.
tips: Action = reaction (same size, opposite direction).

similar_questions.stem: A book rests on a table and pushes down with 5 N. The table pushes up on the book with
explanation_steps: By Newton's third law the reaction is equal: 5 N upwards.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.D: electrons are found in the nucleus

explanation_steps: The nucleus contains protons (positive) and neutrons (no charge). So the nucleus is positively charged.
Protons are in the nucleus, not in the shell. Electrons are in the shells, not in the nucleus. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 74-75)
questions.explain_simple: The nucleus has protons, so it is positive.
tips: Nucleus = protons (+) and neutrons (0). Shells = electrons (−).

similar_questions.stem: Which particle has no electric charge?
explanation_steps: The neutron is neutral: it has no charge.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 3 – The Structure of the Atom

questions.stem: The electronic configuration of chlorine atom is given by 2, 8, 7, then the number of its electrons is
explanation_steps: The configuration 2, 8, 7 means: 2 electrons in the first shell, 8 in the second and 7 in the third.
Total electrons = 2 + 8 + 7 = 17. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 78)
questions.explain_simple: Add the numbers: 2 + 8 + 7 = 17 electrons.
tips: Total electrons = sum of the electrons in all shells.

similar_questions.stem: Sodium has the configuration 2, 8, 1. How many electrons does it have?
explanation_steps: 2 + 8 + 1 = 11 electrons.

textbook_ref.topic: 3.3 Arrangement of subatomic particles in the atom
textbook_ref.subject: Science

questions.stem: In the reaction C + O₂ → CO₂, which statement is true?
explanation_steps: Reactants are on the left: C and O₂ (two reactants). The product is on the right: CO₂.
So A and C are wrong (there are two reactants) and D is wrong. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 92)
questions.explain_simple: CO₂ is after the arrow, so it is the product.
tips: Left of arrow: reactants. Right of arrow: products.

similar_questions.stem: In 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, the product is
explanation_steps: Water (H₂O) is on the right side, so it is the product.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 4 – Chemical Reactions and the Periodic Table

questions.stem: Which of the following is false about metallic elements?

options.D: metals are poor conductor of electricity

explanation_steps: Metals are shiny, malleable (can be hammered into sheets), ductile and sonorous (they ring when hit).
Metals conduct heat and electricity WELL. So 'poor conductor of electricity' is false. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 93)
questions.explain_simple: Metals are good conductors of electricity. So D is false.
tips: Metals: shiny, malleable, ductile, sonorous, good conductors.

similar_questions.stem: Copper is used to make electric wires because it is
explanation_steps: Copper is a metal that conducts electricity very well.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 4 – Chemical Reactions and the Periodic Table

questions.stem: The transfer of heat by current of liquids and gases is:
explanation_steps: In liquids and gases, warm parts rise and cool parts sink. This makes a current that carries heat.
This is convection. Conduction is in solids; radiation needs no matter. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 108)
questions.explain_simple: Heat carried by moving liquid or gas is convection.
tips: Convection = heat moved by currents in fluids.

similar_questions.stem: Sea breezes near the coast are caused by
explanation_steps: Warm air over land rises and cool air from the sea moves in: a convection current.

questions.stem: An inclined plane with one or two slopping sides is called a:
explanation_steps: A wedge is an inclined plane with one or two sloping sides, for example an axe blade or a knife.
A screw is an inclined plane wound around a rod. Levers and pulleys are other simple machines. Answer: D.
(The paper prints 'slopping'; it means 'sloping'.)
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 16-17)
questions.explain_simple: A wedge is like a moving inclined plane with sloping sides, for example an axe.
tips: Axe, knife, nail tip = wedges.

similar_questions.stem: An inclined plane wrapped around a rod is a
explanation_steps: A screw is an inclined plane wound round a cylinder.

questions.stem: The simplest kind of substance which cannot be divided into simpler substances by chemical means is called:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'An element is the simplest kind of substance which can not be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.'
A compound can be broken down chemically; a mixture can be separated physically. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: An element is the simplest substance. It cannot be broken down.
tips: Element = one kind of atom only.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these is an element?
explanation_steps: Oxygen is made of only oxygen atoms, so it is an element.

questions.stem: Sara used an instrument to measure the temperature of water in a glass (Figure 5). The instrument she used is called
questions.image_alt: Figure 5: a Celsius thermometer standing in a glass of water. A magnified circle shows the scale from 20 to 30; the liquid column ends at the middle mark, 25 °C.
explanation_steps: Temperature is measured with a thermometer. The figure shows a thermometer in °C.
A barometer measures air pressure, a beam balance measures mass, and a ruler measures length. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 119-121)
questions.explain_simple: A thermometer measures temperature.
tips: thermo = heat; meter = measure.

similar_questions.stem: Which instrument measures air pressure?
explanation_steps: A barometer measures air pressure.

questions.stem: What is the temperature of the water in the glass (Figure 5) in degree Fahrenheit (°F)?
questions.image_alt: Figure 5 (same as question 26): the thermometer in the glass reads 25 °C (liquid column halfway between 20 and 30).
explanation_steps: Read the thermometer: the liquid ends at the long mark halfway between 20 and 30, so the water is 25 °C.
Change to Fahrenheit: TF = (9/5) × 25 + 32 = 45 + 32 = 77 °F. Answer: C.
(25 is the Celsius reading, not the Fahrenheit value.)
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 122)
tips: First read °C carefully, then use °F = 9/5 × °C + 32.

similar_questions.stem: Water is at 10 °C. What is this in °F?

questions.stem: When a force of 20 N moves a box to a distance of 4 meters, the work done is:
explanation_steps: Work = force × distance = 20 N × 4 m = 80 J.
The unit of work is the joule (J), not the newton, so A is wrong. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 59)
questions.explain_simple: Work = 20 × 4 = 80 joules.
tips: Check the unit too: work is in joules (J).

similar_questions.stem: A girl lifts a box with a force of 15 N through 2 m. The work done is
explanation_steps: W = 15 × 2 = 30 J (joules).

questions.stem: Cattle mainly raised for their meat are:
explanation_steps: The textbook groups cattle into dairy cattle (milk), beef cattle (meat) and work cattle (ploughing, carrying).
'Beef cattle – raised for meat.' Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Cattle kept for meat are beef cattle.
tips: Dairy = milk; beef = meat; work = ploughing.

similar_questions.stem: Cattle kept mainly to give milk are called
explanation_steps: Dairy cattle are raised for milk.

questions.stem: Plants competing with crops for nutrients, water, space and light are called:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'Weeds compete with crops for nutrients, water, space and light.'
Pests are animals (like insects) that damage crops; pesticides are chemicals; cereals are crops. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Unwanted plants that compete with crops are weeds.
tips: Weed = a plant growing where it is not wanted.

similar_questions.stem: One way to control weeds is
explanation_steps: Weeds can be removed by hand picking (physical means) or with chemicals.

questions.stem: In the food chain: grass → sheep → hyena.
explanation_steps: Grass is the producer (it makes food), not a decomposer.
The sheep eats grass (herbivore). The hyena eats the sheep (meat), so it is a carnivore.
There is no cow in this chain (option B is a slip in the paper), and hyenas eat meat, not plants. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 126-128)
questions.explain_simple: The hyena eats the sheep. An animal that eats meat is a carnivore.
tips: First in a chain = producer; plant eater = herbivore; meat eater = carnivore.

similar_questions.stem: In the chain maize → rat → snake → eagle, the producer is
explanation_steps: Maize is a green plant that makes its own food.

questions.stem: Rotation of the Earth:
explanation_steps: Rotation is the spinning of the Earth on its axis. One rotation takes about 24 hours.
The side facing the Sun has day; the other side has night. So rotation forms day and night.
Moving around the Sun (365¼ days) is revolution, which with the tilted axis gives the seasons. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 148)
questions.explain_simple: The Earth spins on its axis. This gives us day and night.
tips: Rotation (spin, 24 h) → day and night. Revolution (around the Sun, 365¼ days) → seasons.

similar_questions.stem: How long does the Earth take to go once around the Sun?
explanation_steps: One revolution around the Sun takes about 365¼ days (one year).

questions.stem: Lamps and electrical devices in houses are operated independently, because

options.A: current flows in the same path

explanation_steps: In a parallel circuit each lamp has its own path to the source. You can switch one lamp on or off without affecting the others.
In a series circuit there is only one path: if one lamp is off, all go off.
House wiring is parallel. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 169)
questions.explain_simple: House lamps are connected in parallel, so each one works alone.
tips: Parallel = many paths (independent). Series = one path (all together).

similar_questions.stem: Three bulbs are in series. One bulb breaks. What happens to the others?
explanation_steps: In series there is only one path, so the circuit is broken and all bulbs go off.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 8 – Introduction to Electricity and Magnetism

questions.stem: In figure 6, egg cells are produced in:
questions.image_alt: Figure 6: the female reproductive organs. 1 points to a round ovary at the end of a tube, 2 to the curved fallopian tube, 3 to the womb (uterus) in the middle, and 4 to the vagina at the bottom.
explanation_steps: Figure 6 shows the female reproductive organs.
Structure 1 is the round ovary at the end of the tube; 2 is the fallopian tube; 3 is the womb (uterus); 4 is the vagina.
Egg cells (ova) are produced in the ovaries. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 187; Science Grade 8, p. 23)
questions.explain_simple: Eggs are made in the ovary. The ovary is structure 1.
tips: Ovary – makes eggs; fallopian tube – carries eggs; womb – baby grows.

similar_questions.stem: In the same figure, where does a baby grow during pregnancy?
explanation_steps: Structure 3 is the womb (uterus), where the baby grows.

questions.stem: A fruit, for example tomato, is also called a matured:
explanation_steps: After fertilization, the ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit.
The textbook says: 'A matured ovule is called a seed while a matured ovary that contains seeds is called a fruit.' Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: A fruit is a grown ovary with seeds inside.
tips: Ovule → seed. Ovary → fruit.

similar_questions.stem: After fertilization, a matured ovule becomes a
explanation_steps: A matured ovule is a seed.

questions.stem: Cell division mitosis occurs in:
explanation_steps: Mitosis occurs only in body cells (muscle, skin, bone and others).
Egg cells, sperm cells and pollen grains are sex cells, made by meiosis. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 133)
questions.explain_simple: Muscle cells are body cells. Body cells divide by mitosis.
tips: Body cells → mitosis. Sex cells → meiosis.

similar_questions.stem: In which organ does meiosis take place?
explanation_steps: Meiosis happens in the testes and ovaries to make sex cells.

questions.stem: Identify an example of acquired trait in humans.
explanation_steps: Acquired traits are learned or come from the environment during life.
Swimming is a skill you learn, so it is acquired. Nose structure, eye colour and ear structure are inherited from parents. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 141)
questions.explain_simple: Swimming is learned. It is an acquired trait.
tips: Can you learn it or get it by an accident? → acquired.

similar_questions.stem: Which is an inherited trait?
explanation_steps: Skin colour is passed from parents through genes.

questions.stem: Dusting of pollen grains on the stigma of a flower is:
explanation_steps: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains to the stigma. Fertilization is a later step, so B is wrong.
'Dusting' means putting pollen on the stigma on purpose, by hand or with a brush. When people do it, it is artificial pollination.
The stem does not say if the pollen comes from the same flower or another plant, so we cannot choose self or cross pollination. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 205)
questions.explain_simple: When people put (dust) pollen on a stigma by hand, it is artificial pollination.
tips: Look for clues: 'by hand' or 'dusting' = artificial.

similar_questions.stem: A farmer takes pollen from one maize plant and puts it on another maize plant by hand. This is
explanation_steps: Done by a person (artificial) and between two plants (cross).

questions.review_flag: Unclear stem: 'dusting of pollen grains on the stigma' does not say whether the pollen comes from the same flower or another plant, or who does it. Keyed D (artificial pollination), because 'dusting' describes hand pollination (as in 2012 Q43). Teacher to confirm.

questions.stem: A force that every object exerts on every other object is:
explanation_steps: Every object pulls every other object with a force of attraction. This force is gravity (gravitational force).
Mass, acceleration and velocity are not forces. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 151)
questions.explain_simple: All objects pull each other. This pull is gravity.
tips: Gravity = the pull between all masses.

similar_questions.stem: Why does a ball fall back to the ground?
explanation_steps: The Earth's gravity pulls the ball down.

questions.stem: A gas layer that protects life on earth from ultraviolet rays is:
explanation_steps: The stratosphere contains a gas called ozone.
The textbook says: 'The ozone layer protects life on earth from the harmful ultraviolet rays of the sun.' Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: The ozone layer stops harmful ultraviolet rays from the Sun.
tips: Ozone layer = sunscreen of the Earth (in the stratosphere).

similar_questions.stem: In which layer of the atmosphere is the ozone layer found?
explanation_steps: The ozone layer is in the stratosphere.

questions.stem: The four major layers of atmosphere from the lowest to the uppermost are:
explanation_steps: From the ground up: troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere.
C gives the same layers but from the top down. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 148)
questions.explain_simple: From the bottom: troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere.
tips: Memory: 'The Sun Makes Things' warm → T, S, M, T.

similar_questions.stem: Which layer of the atmosphere is the lowest?
explanation_steps: The troposphere is the lowest layer, where we live.

questions.stem: The water that falls on the earth as rain is called:
explanation_steps: In the water cycle, water vapour condenses to form clouds. Then water falls from the clouds as rain (or snow, hail).
Water falling to the earth is called precipitation. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 170)
questions.explain_simple: Rain falling from clouds is called precipitation.
tips: Water cycle: evaporation → condensation → precipitation.

similar_questions.stem: In the water cycle, water from the sea changing into water vapour is
explanation_steps: Liquid water becoming vapour because of the Sun's heat is evaporation.

questions.stem: Nearly three-quarter of the earth's surface is:
explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'Water covers nearly three-quarters of the earth's surface.'
So nearly 3/4 of the surface is covered by water bodies (oceans, seas, lakes, rivers). Answer: B.
C (salty water) is also almost true, because oceans and seas (salty) cover about 71% of the surface. The textbook wording is 'water', so B is keyed and C is also accepted.
questions.explain_simple: Water covers nearly three-quarters of the Earth's surface.
tips: 3/4 of the surface = water; 97% of that water = salty.

similar_questions.stem: Most of the water on the Earth is found in
explanation_steps: Oceans and seas hold about 97% of the Earth's water.

questions.review_flag: Two defensible options: B 'water body' matches the textbook sentence ('Water covers nearly three-quarters of the earth's surface'), but C 'salty water' is also nearly true (oceans and seas cover about 71% of the surface). Keyed B, C also accepted. Teacher to decide.

questions.stem: The poisonous gas produced by vehicles in their exhaust is called:
explanation_steps: Car engines give out carbon monoxide (CO) in their exhaust. It is a very poisonous gas.
Oxygen and nitrogen are normal gases of the air. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 195)
questions.explain_simple: Cars give out carbon monoxide. It is poisonous.
tips: CO (carbon monoxide) = poison from car exhaust and charcoal fires in closed rooms.

similar_questions.stem: Which gas from factories causes acid rain?
explanation_steps: Sulphur dioxide mixes with rain water and forms acid rain.

questions.stem: Filtration is a method of:

options.A: removing solid particles from water using clean cloth
options.B: making water safe for drinking using clean cloth
options.C: throwing rubbish into clean water using clean cloth
options.D: boiling clean water to kill micro-organisms

explanation_steps: The textbook says: 'Sand and other solid particles can be removed from water by filtration', for example with a clean cloth.
Filtration makes water clean but not safe: germs can still pass. Killing germs needs boiling or chlorine. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Filtration removes dirt from water. It does not kill germs.
tips: Filter = clean. Boil = safe.

similar_questions.stem: Which method kills germs in water?
explanation_steps: Boiling for 10–15 minutes kills micro-organisms.

questions.stem: Chemicals used to kill weeds are called:
explanation_steps: Pesticides are named by what they kill: insecticides kill insects, rodenticides kill rats and mice, fungicides kill fungi.
Herbicides kill weeds (unwanted plants). Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 192; Science Grade 7, p. 112)
questions.explain_simple: Herbicides kill weeds.
tips: herb = plant; insect-icide = insect killer; -cide = killer.

similar_questions.stem: Farmers spray a chemical to kill insects on their crops. The chemical is
explanation_steps: Insecticides kill insects.

questions.stem: An increase in the average temperature of the earth causes:
explanation_steps: An increase in the average temperature of the earth is global warming.
Global warming melts ice at the poles and makes the sea level RISE (not drop). Deserts get bigger, not smaller. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 197)
questions.explain_simple: A warmer Earth melts the ice at the poles.
tips: Global warming → ice melts → sea level rises → floods.

similar_questions.stem: Which gas is the main cause of global warming?
explanation_steps: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere.

questions.stem: If sound is heard from a distance of 1,320 m in 4 seconds, its speed is:
explanation_steps: Speed = distance ÷ time.
v = 1320 m ÷ 4 s = 330 m/s. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 208-209)
tips: v = s ÷ t.

similar_questions.stem: Sound travels 680 m in 2 s. What is its speed?

questions.stem: In which order does sound travel from the fastest to the lowest?
explanation_steps: Sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids and slowest in gases.
Example: steel 5940 m/s, water 1483 m/s, air 343 m/s. Answer: C.
(The paper writes 'lowest'; it means 'slowest'.)
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 209)
questions.explain_simple: Sound is fastest in solids, then liquids, then gases.
tips: Sound speed: solid > liquid > gas.

similar_questions.stem: In which material does sound travel slowest?
explanation_steps: Air is a gas, and sound travels slowest in gases.

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct?

options.A: echo is a reflection of sound
options.B: echo is produced in soft material

explanation_steps: An echo is a reflected sound: sound bounces back from a hard surface like a wall or a cliff.
Soft materials absorb sound, so they do not make good echoes. Sound (and so an echo) cannot travel through a vacuum. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 212)
questions.explain_simple: An echo is sound that bounces back.
tips: Echo = reflection of sound from hard surfaces.

similar_questions.stem: Echoes are heard best when sound hits
explanation_steps: Hard surfaces reflect sound well, so echoes are strong.
